chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Durays, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who commanded his slave-girl to enter the state of Ihram at the same time, so she entered Ihram while he had not yet entered Ihram, and he had intercourse with her after she had entered Ihram. He said: 'He commands her to perform Ghusl, then she enters Ihram, and there is no penalty upon him.'

Because this report is construed upon the basis that she had not yet recited the Talbiyah, for when the matter is as we mentioned, the penalty does not become obligatory upon him, and we have previously established that. And if a man has intercourse before the Tawaf al-Ziyarah, he must slaughter a camel, then perform Tawaf; if he cannot, then a cow or a sheep, as narrated.

key_terms.إحرام: State of consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.طواف الزيارة: Tawaf al-Ziyarah (the specific circumambulation of Hajj)

ai.seo_question: What is the penalty for a man who has intercourse with his slave-girl after she has entered Ihram but he has not?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that if a master commands his slave-girl to enter Ihram and she does so, but he has not yet entered, and they have intercourse, she must perform Ghusl and renew her Ihram while he incurs no penalty, provided she had not yet recited the Talbiyah. This ruling highlights the distinction between the obligation of Ihram and the specific act of Talbiyah in determining liability for minor infractions. Furthermore, it establishes that if intercourse occurs before Tawaf al-Ziyarah, the man must sacrifice an animal (camel, cow, or sheep) before completing the pilgrimage rites.
